# Fairpractice ABA Therapy (`fairpractice-aba-therapy`)

Checks ABA therapy billing against authorizations: sessions with no authorization, units over the total or weekly authorized amount, units above what the session minutes support, codes billed by a technician that need a BCBA, supervision below your monthly minimum, and authorizations ending with hours unused. Client names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice ABA Therapy never submits or changes claims. Fairpractice ABA Therapy never requests authorizations from a payer.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-aba-therapy demo
npx -y fairpractice-aba-therapy mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bright Steps ABA (a made-up clinic), made-up clients and staff. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`authorizations.csv`](fixtures/authorizations.csv) and [`sessions-2026-q4.csv`](fixtures/sessions-2026-q4.csv): Planted: 44 units in the week of November 2 against a 40-unit weekly limit, and 9 units billed for a 2-hour session that supports 8 (C1); a session after the authorization ended, with no supervision that month (C2); a supervision code billed by a technician, no BCBA supervision that month, and an authorization ending December 10 with most units unused (C3); and 24 units against a 20-unit authorization (C4).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 15-minute units, a 5% monthly supervision minimum (check your payer and certification rules) and example unit rates. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `aba_check` | List sessions with no or exhausted authorization, unit and role problems, low supervision and authorizations ending unused. | runs |
| `aba_write_report` | Write aba.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and aba.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/aba). | runs |
| `aba_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `aba_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `aba_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `aba_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairpractice ABA Therapy never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `auth_request_submit` | Fairpractice ABA Therapy never requests authorizations from a payer. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `aba_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sessions` (required) | Session or claim lines under --root: client, date, start and end times or minutes, code, units, provider and provider role, authorization number |
| `authorizations` (required) | Authorization log: client, authorization number, code (blank for all), units, weekly units, start and end |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: unit_minutes, supervision_pct, direct_codes, supervision_codes, qualified_only_codes, rates, warn_days, unused_pct |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-aba-therapy inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Sessions (`sessions`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `start` | text | Start, Start Time, Time In, From Time |
| `end` | text | End, End Time, Time Out, To Time |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `provider` | text (masked) | Provider, Rendering Provider, Rendering, Clinician, Therapist, Physician, Doctor, Practitioner |
| `provider_role` | text | Provider Role, Role, Credential, Provider Credential, Staff Type |
| `auth_number` | text | Auth #, Auth Number, Authorization, Authorization #, Auth ID, PA # |

### Authorizations (`authorizations`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` (required) | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `auth_number` | text | Auth #, Auth Number, Authorization, Authorization #, Auth ID, PA # |
| `cpt` | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Authorized Units, Approved Units, Total Units |
| `weekly_units` | number | Weekly Units, Units per Week, Weekly Limit, Max per Week |
| `start` (required) | date | Start, Start Date, From, Effective, Auth Start |
| `end` | date | End, End Date, Through, Thru, Expires, Auth End |

## Settings file (`aba_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `unit_minutes` | Minutes in one unit; default 15 |
| `supervision_pct` | Minimum supervision as a percent of technician direct time per client per month (certification and payer minimums vary); default 5 |
| `direct_codes` | Codes for technician direct treatment; default 97153, 97154 |
| `supervision_codes` | Codes that count as supervision when a BCBA bills them; default 97155 |
| `qualified_only_codes` | Codes only a qualified professional may bill; default 97151, 97155, 97156, 97157 |
| `rates` | Expected payment per unit by code, for dollar totals |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn about authorizations ending; default 30 |
| `unused_pct` | Percent unused at which an ending authorization is listed; default 25 |

## Memory

`aba_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `aba_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-aba-therapy": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-aba-therapy",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-aba-therapy -- npx -y fairpractice-aba-therapy mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-aba-therapy tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-aba-therapy sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-aba-therapy inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-aba-therapy call aba_check '{"sessions":"<sessions>","authorizations":"<authorizations>"}'
fairpractice-aba-therapy eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-aba-therapy demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
